title: Center symmetry on the lattice: twist invariance, Polyakov-loop covariance and the ⟨χ(P)⟩ = 0 selection rule
claim: For any group G, central element z, d, L ≥ 1 and direction τ on the periodic lattice (ℤ/Lℤ)^d, the Lean theorem Contribution.result proves four things. (1) The center twist multiplies every τ-link leaving one slice x_τ = t₀ by z. It leaves every plaquette, and hence every plaquette action (Wilson or otherwise, no class-function hypothesis), exactly invariant. (2) The Polyakov loop P_b (from accepted pr-12) is gauge covariant, P_b(gU) = g_b P_b(U) g_b⁻¹. The twist of the slice through b multiplies it by z, P_b ↦ z P_b. So χ(P_b) is gauge invariant for class functions χ, yet charged under the center. (3) Selection rule: let E be any ℂ-linear expectation on observables that is invariant under the twist. If χ(z h) = ω χ(h) with ω ≠ 1 (e.g. χ = tr in the fundamental of SU(N), z = e^{2πi/N}), then E(χ∘P_b) = 0. This is the lattice form of the statement that an unbroken center symmetry forces a vanishing Polyakov-loop expectation, the classic confinement order parameter ('t Hooft; Svetitsky–Yaffe). (4) Applying pr-12's axial gauge to the twisted configuration, the residual last-slice link equals z times the original Polyakov loop. The twist is visible exactly in the gauge-fixed residual data. Item (2) also supplies the precise covariance statement that the pr-12 review asked for: the Polyakov element is covariant by conjugation, and its class-function evaluations are invariant.
novelty: This builds on accepted track results pr-12 (lines, Polyakov loops, axial gauge; its theorem is used in part (4)) and pr-10 (plaquettes, gauge action, plaquette actions). No accepted track contribution treats center symmetry. The mathematics is classical ('t Hooft 1978; Svetitsky–Yaffe 1982; Polyakov 1978). In the external Lean library lgt (Douglas), a search of commit b8793ccf found no center, Polyakov or twist statements. New relative to the track: an exact formal center twist for arbitrary groups; invariance of all plaquette actions under it; gauge covariance of Polyakov loops; their exact center charge; the abstract linear-expectation selection rule; and the combination with the pr-12 axial gauge.

limitations: This is classical, configuration-level infrastructure. The expectation E in (3) is an arbitrary twist-invariant linear functional. The Haar/Wilson Gibbs measure is not constructed here, and its twist invariance is not proved; that needs Haar measure invariance under multiplication by z. The rule therefore gives ⟨χ(P)⟩ = 0 only once such a measure-level invariance is supplied, and it says nothing about spontaneous breaking, the deconfinement transition or area-law confinement. The twist is stated for a single slice; for (2)–(3) the slice passes through the Polyakov base point. Nothing here constructs the continuum theory or proves a mass gap.
